message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • General limit: 55 mph on rural roads, 45 mph on urban roads.
• 70 mph on interstate highways (except where posted otherwise).
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if a school bus is present). | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Regulations | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• The “no‑seat‑belt” law applies to all vehicles. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited (unless using a hands‑free system).
• Texting while driving is illegal. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02%).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has the right of way.
• Stop signs: come to a full stop before proceeding. | Texas Transportation Code §§545.021–545.023 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Cannot pass a stopped school bus until the bus’s stop sign is retracted. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals at least 100 ft before changing lanes.
• Do not exceed the speed limit when overtaking. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk, fire hydrant, or intersection.
• Parking on sidewalks is prohibited unless marked. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) | | **Toll Roads & Bridges** | • Texas has several toll roads (e.g., Sam Houston Tollway, LBJ Freeway).
• Toll rates vary by vehicle type and time of day. | TxDOT Toll Operations | | **Emergency Vehicle Rules** | • Drivers must yield to emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens.
• Must pull over to the right side of the road and stop. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Bicyclists must ride in the lane if one exists; otherwise, they may ride on the shoulder.
• Motorcycles must use the lane and signal. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Penalties & Enforcement** | • Fines, points on your driving record, license suspension, and possible jail time.
• Texas Highway Patrol and local police enforce these laws. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official website for traffic regulations, road conditions, and updates. 2. **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)** – For registration, licensing, and inspection requirements. 3. **Texas Transportation Code** – The legal text governing all traffic laws. 4. **Local County Courts** – For specific local ordinances (e.g., city parking rules). --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always obey posted speed limits** – they’re designed for safety. - **Keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a legal requirement and saves lives. - **Avoid distractions** – especially cell‑phone use while driving. - **Respect school bus rules** – they’re there to protect children. - **Use signals early** – give other drivers enough time to react. - **Stay alert for toll roads** – know the payment options (e‑Toll, toll tags). Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law, recent changes, or how to handle a particular traffic situation in Texas!
